subject: surveying
intro: Surveying is the licensed profession that fixes where everything is — boundaries, buildings and infrastructure — feeding construction, mapping, geodesy and the land-law system that property runs on.

roles.title: Surveyors
roles.what: Make exact measurements and determine property boundaries, providing data on the shape, contour, location, elevation and dimension of land features for engineering, mapmaking, mining, land evaluation and construction.
roles.where: The syllabus is the FS exam blueprint: surveying mathematics with error and uncertainty, theodolites and total stations, levelling, GNSS positioning, and the boundary and land law unit's deeds, monuments and retracement principles.

roles.title: Surveying and Mapping Technicians
roles.what: Perform surveying and mapping duties under the direction of surveyors and engineers, obtaining data for construction, mapmaking and boundary location, and creating maps from survey notes, aerial photography and satellite data.
roles.where: The measurement instruments unit — total stations, EDM, levelling — and the topographic and construction surveying unit's staking and as-built work are the daily field tasks, with GIS integration from the modern practice unit on the office side.

roles.title: Cartographers and Photogrammetrists
roles.what: Collect, analyse and interpret geographic information from geodetic surveys, aerial photographs and satellite data to prepare maps and other spatial data in digital or graphic form, often working within GIS.
roles.where: The drone photogrammetry, LiDAR and GIS topics in the modern practice unit are precisely this occupation's data engines, with geodesy basics and GNSS differential positioning from earlier units providing the accuracy foundation.

roles.title: Civil Engineers
roles.what: Plan, design and oversee the construction and maintenance of building structures and infrastructure such as roads, railroads, airports, bridges, dams, pipelines and water and sewage systems.
roles.where: Construction staking and as-built surveys from the topographic unit are how civil projects get built in the right place, and control networks and error analysis from the positioning units underpin every design coordinate they use.
